sam: quick heads-up — seeing a reproducible stall where continuous-batching+merge causes a KV-cache head-of-line hold and mem growth for long contexts. flamegraph spikes in kv_pager::evict and contbatch::merge_wait.

jordan: repro steps + kernel config?

sam: repro: run local perf harness with --long-context 64k, --batch-window-ms 20, mixed-prefix workload (50/50 short/long). command: `./perf_run --profile kv --iters 200 --long-context`
expected: steady latency and stable resident mem.
actual: p95 jumps from 120ms -> 1.2s after ~3k requests, resident grows ~1.1GB.

maria: do you see many page faults or reclaim churn? any evict thrash logs?

sam: yes — /proc/vmstat shows pgfault/s spike aligned with the stall. kernel selectors look normal; we saw increased calls to async_evict and many small fragments left behind. pasted minimal log: ```EVICT hit slab=kv_frag size=64k free=12/1024; reclaim=async; waiting merges=7```

anita: hypothesis: merge is combining batches that reference both hot and cold KV shards. long-context requests pin big prefix chains in memory; when merged with short ones we get HOL blocking while evict tries to shuffle fragments. fragmentation + delayed sub-batch processing -> mem growth.

jordan: that matches an earlier note — merge heuristics ignore kv residency. short-term mitigation: cap merged token count or avoid merging across prefix-hash boundaries. can you test lowering batch-window?

sam: did a quick toggle: batch-window 20ms -> 5ms, p95 drops to ~210ms, resident drops by ~350MB in that run. not perfect but reduces HOL. numbers: before: p95=1.2s mem=4.1GB; after: p95=210ms mem=3.75GB.

perf-bot: CI regression detected on master at commit abc1234 — increase in kv_pager tail latency by +18% vs baseline (see perf/kv/longctx/bench).

anita: thanks — we should add a guard in contbatch merge: check active_kv_residency per-request and prefer same-residency groups. quick patch idea: compute lightweight residency-key (hot/cold) from last-touch counters and avoid merging across types.

maria: can we also evict asynchronously earlier when merged batches contain long-context markers? maybe prefetch/lock ordering tweak so evict doesn't block merged fast requests.

jordan: I'll open ENGRT-5496 and attach the repro, flamegraphs, and the quick numbers. @sam can you add heaptrack sample and top-10 symbols from the run?

sam: will run heaptrack + send logs later today. thanks all. :thumbsup:
